section: Applications of radioisotopes in agriculture, medicine and industry
subsections: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use
Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT
Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: Which one of the following radioisotopes is supplied by BRIT as sodium iodide for the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid disorders?
accepted.x: Iodine-131 emits beta and gamma radiation and is supplied by BRIT as sodium iodide for thyroid diagnosis and treatment.
accepted.tq: Match the isotope with its characteristic organ-related application.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Phosphorus-32 is used in agriculture mainly for studying:
o: The rate of photosynthesis in leaves
The uptake of phosphorus by plants
accepted.x: Phosphorus-32 acts as a tracer for studying phosphorus uptake by plants.
accepted.tq: Use the tracer application to distinguish an isotope from disease-treatment uses.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Sodium-24 is particularly useful for studying:
accepted.x: Sodium-24 emits gamma radiation and is used in blood-flow and circulation studies; it can also help detect pipeline leaks.
accepted.tq: Identify the isotope from its specific diagnostic application.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Which of the following radioisotopes is associated with pipeline leak detection as well as blood-flow studies?
accepted.x: Sodium-24 is used for blood-flow and circulation studies and also for detecting leaks in pipelines.
accepted.tq: Connect one isotope with two related tracer applications.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Technetium-99m:
1. It is the most widely used diagnostic isotope.
2. It is used for imaging the heart, brain, bones and lungs.
3. It is a principal isotope used in radioimmunoassay to measure hormones in blood.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Technetium-99m is the most widely used diagnostic isotope and is used in imaging the heart, brain, bones and lungs. Radioimmunoassay is a technique, not the principal stated use of Technetium-99m.
accepted.tq: Separate the isotope’s established imaging uses from the broader radioimmunoassay technique.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Iron-59 is used chiefly in studies relating to:
accepted.x: Iron-59 emits beta and gamma radiation and is used to study iron metabolism and anaemia.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct isotope–clinical study pair.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Arsenic-74 emits positrons and is used for locating brain tumours. Iron-59 concerns iron metabolism, Sodium-24 concerns blood flow, and Carbon-14 is used for dating organic material.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure isotope–use pair and eliminate swapped applications.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Radioimmunoassay is a technique used to measure minute quantities of which of the following in blood?
o: Only red blood cells and platelets
accepted.x: Radioimmunoassay uses radioisotopes to measure minute quantities of hormones, enzymes and drugs in blood.
accepted.tq: Recognise the exact analytes associated with a specialised diagnostic technique.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the new targeted radionuclide therapy 177Lu-DOTA-FAPI-2286 is correct?
o: It is used exclusively for dating organic material.
It is a gamma irradiator for medical devices.
It is in routine clinical use.
It is the fuel of the KAMINI reactor.
accepted.x: 177Lu-DOTA-FAPI-2286 is a targeted radionuclide therapy introduced into routine clinical practice.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a newly introduced clinical therapy from institutions and facilities.
accepted.sec: Medical radioisotopes - isotope, radiation and use

accepted.s: Brachytherapy differs from teletherapy in that brachytherapy involves:
o: Detecting positrons emitted from injected glucose
Using only an external Co-60 beam from a distant unit
Using gamma emitters only for blood-flow studies
Placing a sealed radiation source inside or next to the tumour
accepted.x: Brachytherapy places a sealed source, such as Ir-192 or I-125 seeds, inside or adjacent to the tumour. Teletherapy is external-beam treatment, commonly using a Co-60 unit.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar radiation-treatment modalities by their source location.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: Which of the following is primarily used as a positron emitter in PET imaging?
accepted.x: PET mainly uses the positron emitter F-18 FDG. Tc-99m is commonly associated with SPECT, while Co-60 is used in teletherapy.
accepted.tq: Separate PET positron emitters from SPECT and therapy sources.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: SPECT imaging generally uses:
o: Ultrasound waves from a medical cyclotron
Single gamma emitters such as Technetium-99m
Only positron emitters such as F-18 FDG
accepted.x: SPECT uses single gamma emitters, particularly Technetium-99m. PET, in contrast, mainly uses positron emitters such as F-18 FDG.
accepted.tq: Compare the radiation emitted in PET and SPECT rather than memorising the names alone.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: The 30 MeV Medical Cyclotron located at Kolkata is associated with the commercial production of:
accepted.x: The 30 MeV Medical Cyclotron at Kolkata produces F-18 FDG commercially for PET applications and delivers doses to hospitals.
accepted.tq: Link a specialised facility with its distinctive product.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the 30 MeV Medical Cyclotron, Kolkata is correct?
o: It was renamed from AEET in 1967.
It sterilised 1.53 crore medical devices by September 2025.
It delivered 371 Ci of FDG doses to hospitals.
It is the only U-233-fuelled research reactor in India.
accepted.x: The Kolkata Medical Cyclotron produced FDG commercially and delivered 371 Ci of doses to hospitals. The other statements refer to the Indore plant, BARC’s institutional history and KAMINI respectively.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive number to distinguish closely related nuclear facilities.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Radiotherapy may use gamma rays, X-rays or beta emitters.
2. Gamma rays have applications in nuclear medicine apart from radiotherapy.
3. PET and SPECT both principally use the same type of radioactive emission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Radiotherapy can use gamma rays, X-rays or beta emitters, and gamma rays also underpin nuclear medicine. Statement 3 is false because PET mainly uses positron emitters, whereas SPECT uses single gamma emitters.
accepted.tq: Find the false comparison by distinguishing PET from SPECT.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: The Tata Memorial Centre serves as the Anchor Centre for the IAEA initiative known as:
accepted.x: Tata Memorial Centre is the Anchor Centre for the International Atomic Energy Agency’s ‘Rays of Hope’ initiative.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with the exact international initiative.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: The National Cancer Grid, established in 2012, is stated to treat approximately:
o: 7.5 lakh or more new patients a year
accepted.x: The National Cancer Grid, established in 2012, treats more than 7.5 lakh new patients annually and addresses over 60% of India’s cancer burden.
accepted.tq: Read the year and scale together instead of confusing it with facility-capacity figures.
accepted.sec: Radiation therapy - radon, brachytherapy, PET and SPECT

accepted.s: BRIT is best described as:
o: An international agency regulating PET scans
An industrial unit of the Department of Atomic Energy dealing with radioisotopes and related technology
A private organisation responsible only for cancer treatment
A research reactor situated at Trombay
accepted.x: BRIT, or the Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology, is an industrial unit of the Department of Atomic Energy involved in radioisotopes, radiopharmaceuticals and isotope technology.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional identity and controlling department.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: The headquarters of the Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology is located at:
accepted.x: BRIT is headquartered at Vashi, Navi Mumbai. Trombay is associated with BARC, while Indore and Kolkata host other radiation-related facilities.
accepted.tq: Use location-based elimination among nearby nuclear institutions.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a product or service associated with BRIT?
accepted.x: BRIT supplies radioimmunoassay kits, radiography cameras and gamma chambers, besides radioisotopes, radiopharmaceuticals and radiation-processing services. Hydroelectric dam construction is unrelated to BRIT.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the institution’s actual product portfolio.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about BARC:
1. It was established in 1954 as the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay.
2. It was renamed BARC in 1967.
3. It is India’s leading producer of radioisotopes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The institution was set up as AEET in 1954, renamed BARC in 1967 and became India’s leading producer of radioisotopes.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional-history statement before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with a BARC research reactor?
o: Dhruva — largest research reactor among those listed
accepted.x: Dhruva is identified as the largest research reactor. Apsara was Asia’s first research reactor, KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor, and FDG production is associated with the Kolkata Medical Cyclotron.
accepted.tq: Use the unique descriptor of each reactor to reject swapped pairings.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. BARC was renamed from AEET.
B. The National Cancer Grid was established.
C. ISOMED 2.0 was completed.
D. The Indore electron-beam plant sterilised 1.53 crore medical devices by September.
accepted.x: BARC was renamed in 1967, the National Cancer Grid was established in 2012, ISOMED 2.0 was completed in May 2025, and the Indore sterilisation figure was reported by September 2025.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest institutional date first, then arrange the later dated developments.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s:
Isotopes used in India are produced at which of the following locations or types of facilities?
1. Trombay research reactors
2. The Kolkata accelerator
3. NPCIL power plants
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India produces isotopes in Trombay research reactors, at the Kolkata accelerator and in NPCIL power plants.
accepted.tq: Test whether all listed production locations belong to the same supply chain.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: India supplies radioisotopes such as Cobalt-60 and Iodine-131 to:
accepted.x: India supplies radioisotopes, including Cobalt-60 and Iodine-131, to more than 40 countries.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the international supply figure from the figures for plants and exports.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: ISOMED 2.0 is correctly described as:
o: A 30 MeV accelerator for producing FDG
A centre for radioimmunoassay blood testing only
A high-intensity gamma irradiator for sterilising healthcare products
accepted.x: ISOMED 2.0 is a high-intensity gamma irradiator for sterilising healthcare products and was completed in May 2025.
accepted.tq: Identify a facility from its technology and purpose.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about ISOMED 2.0 is correct?
o: It exports medical devices to 35 countries.
It is a gamma-processing plant established at Trombay in 1954.
It is the only U-233-fuelled reactor in India.
It is the only land-based stationary facility of its kind in the world.
accepted.x: ISOMED 2.0, completed in May 2025, is described as the only land-based stationary high-intensity gamma irradiator of its kind in the world.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive superlative only where the facility description supports it.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about India’s gamma-processing plants is correct?
o: There were 40 MoUs, 17 commissioned plants and six plants operating.
There were six MoUs, 17 commissioned plants and 35 plants operating.
There were 17 MoUs, six commissioned plants and 40 plants operating.
There were 35 MoUs, six commissioned plants and 17 plants operating.
accepted.x: The reported figures are 17 MoUs, six commissioned plants and 40 gamma-processing plants operating, with BRIT supplying Cobalt-60.
accepted.tq: Keep the three related figures in their correct institutional sequence.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: The electron-beam plant at Indore, Madhya Pradesh, had sterilised what number of medical devices by September 2025?
accepted.x: The Indore electron-beam plant had sterilised 1.53 crore medical devices by September 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the plant’s device count from the ARPF and cancer-grid figures.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: The Indore electron-beam plant exports its sterilised medical devices to:
accepted.x: The Indore plant’s sterilised medical devices are exported to more than 35 countries.
accepted.tq: Separate the plant’s export count from India’s radioisotope-export count.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: ARPF crossed the milestone of one crore devices using:
o: An indigenous 10 MeV, 6 kW linear accelerator
accepted.x: ARPF crossed one crore devices using an indigenous 10 MeV, 6 kW linear accelerator. The 30 MeV medical cyclotron is associated with FDG production in Kolkata.
accepted.tq: Match the facility milestone with its specific equipment specification.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: ARPF — gamma source supplied for teletherapy
accepted.x: KAMINI is identified as the only U-233-fuelled reactor. Dhruva is the largest research reactor, ISOMED 2.0 is a gamma irradiator, and ARPF uses a 10 MeV, 6 kW linear accelerator.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive reactor description and eliminate cross-category substitutions.
accepted.sec: Institutions - BRIT, BARC, radiation processing plants
